proposals.before: Born Song Wentong, he served as a soldier in the Boye Army and was posted to Fengxiang.
proposals.after: Originally surnamed Song with the given name Wentong, he served as a soldier in the Boye Army and was posted to Fengxiang.
proposals.reason: Chinese 本姓宋，名文通 states original surname and given name; 'Born Song Wentong' misreads 姓/名 formula as birth phrasing.

proposals.before: Fengxiang lies too close to Chang’an—strike at him and you court disaster you cannot undo. Another day, even if you killed a scapegoat to appease the warlords, you might not be able to.”
proposals.after: Fengxiang lies too close to Chang’an—strike at him and you court disaster you cannot undo. Another day, even if you wished to execute Chao Cuo to appease the feudal lords, you might not be able to.”
proposals.reason: Chinese names 晁錯 (Chao Cuo); idiomatic 'scapegoat' erases the historical allusion's proper name present in the literal.

proposals.before: Maozhen asked that his son Congmi hold Xingyuan in his stead. Zhaozong moved Maozhen to Shannan West and sent Chancellor Xu Yanruo to Fengxiang.
proposals.after: Maozhen asked that his son Jimi hold Xingyuan in his stead. Zhaozong moved Maozhen to Shannan West and sent Chancellor Xu Yanruo to Fengxiang.
proposals.reason: 繼密 is Jìmì; English Congmi wrongly reads 繼 as Cong (從).

proposals.before: The next year Wang Chongying of Hedong died, and his sons Ke and Gong fought over the circuit.
proposals.after: The next year Wang Chongying of Hezhong died, and his sons Ke and Gong fought over the circuit.
proposals.reason: 河中 is Hezhong, not Hedong (河東); place name mistranslated.

proposals.before: The coup failed, and Jin marched as well. Maozhen, afraid, killed Chancellors Wei Zhaodu and Li Xi, left his adopted son Congpeng with two thousand men as palace guard, and withdrew.
proposals.after: The coup failed, and Jin marched as well. Maozhen, afraid, killed Chancellors Wei Zhaodu and Li Xi, left his adopted son Jipeng with two thousand men as palace guard, and withdrew.
proposals.reason: 繼鵬 is Jìpéng; Congpeng misreads 繼 as Cong.

proposals.before: Jin reached Hedong. Congpeng and Xingyu’s brother Xingshi fought to drag Zhaozong away. Chang’an convulsed. The emperor took refuge at Shimen.
proposals.after: Jin reached Hezhong. Jipeng and Xingyu’s brother Xingshi fought to drag Zhaozong away. Chang’an convulsed. The emperor took refuge at Shimen.
proposals.reason: 河中 is Hezhong not Hedong; 繼鵬 should be Jipeng not Congpeng.

proposals.before: Maozhen marched to E County and killed Congpeng to buy his peace.
proposals.after: Maozhen marched to E County and killed Jipeng to buy his peace.
proposals.reason: 繼鵬 is Jìpéng; Congpeng is a systematic mistranslation of 繼.

proposals.before: Chief Eunuch Han Quanhui and his faction leaned on Maozhen’s power. Maozhen sent his son Congyun with thousands of men into the capital. Backed by Qi’s army, the eunuchs grew brazen and ungovernable.
proposals.after: Chief Eunuch Han Quanhui and his faction leaned on Maozhen’s power. Maozhen sent his son Jiyun with thousands of men into the capital. Backed by Qi’s army, the eunuchs grew brazen and ungovernable.
proposals.reason: 繼筠 is Jìyún; Congyun wrongly reads 繼 as Cong.

proposals.before: In Tianfu 1 (901) Yin called Zhu Wen west. Liang reached Tongzhou. Quanhui and his party, terrified, joined Congyun and dragged Zhaozong to Fengxiang.
proposals.after: In Tianfu 1 (901) Yin called Zhu Wen west. Liang reached Tongzhou. Quanhui and his party, terrified, joined Jiyun and dragged Zhaozong to Fengxiang.
proposals.reason: 繼筠 should be Jiyun, not Congyun.

proposals.before: Cheng Ji of Jingnan then falsely took the surname Guo and was likewise skilled at pacifying Jing-Chu.
proposals.after: Cheng Rui of Jingnan then falsely took the surname Guo and was likewise skilled at pacifying Jing-Chu.
proposals.reason: 成汭 is Cheng Rui (Ruì); Ji is not the standard reading of 汭.

proposals.before: When Wang Chongying of Hedong died, his sons Ke and Gong fought over the circuit. Jin backed Ke; Jian, Wang Xingyu, and Li Maozhen backed Gong.
proposals.after: When Wang Chongying of Hezhong died, his sons Ke and Gong fought over the circuit. Jin backed Ke; Jian, Wang Xingyu, and Li Maozhen backed Gong.
proposals.reason: 河中 is Hezhong, not Hedong (河東).

proposals.before: During Zhu Mei’s revolt, Sijing and Li Sixiao of Bin encamped at Wei Bridge.
proposals.after: During Zhu Mei’s revolt, Sijing and Li Sixiao of Fu Prefecture encamped at Wei Bridge.
proposals.reason: 鄜州 is Fu (or Fu-zhou), not Bin (邠); idiomatic 'Bin' mismatches 鄜州.

proposals.before: Yang Chongben grew up in Li Maozhen’s service, was adopted, took the Li surname and the name Jihui, and was made commissioner of Jingnan.
proposals.after: Yang Chongben grew up in Li Maozhen’s service, was adopted, took the Li surname and the name Jihui, and was made commissioner of the Jingnan (Static Difficulty) army.
proposals.reason: 靜難軍 is the Jingnan Army circuit at Bin, not Jingnan (荊南); keep military-commission clarity.

proposals.before: Li Yanrong of Bin and Li Yanyu of Fang abandoned their posts and ran.
proposals.after: Li Yanrong of Fu Prefecture and Li Yanyu of Fang abandoned their posts and ran.
proposals.reason: Chinese 鄜州 is Fu Prefecture; idiomatic Bin conflates 鄜 with 邠.

proposals.before: Another son, Yunquan, was magistrate of Fushi under Later Jin’s Kaiyun era, then retired home.
proposals.after: Wanjin’s son Yunquan was magistrate of Fushi under Later Jin’s Kaiyun era, then retired home.
proposals.reason: Chinese 萬金子允權 is Wanjin’s son; idiomatic Another son wrongly attaches Yunquan to Wanxing.

proposals.before: Wanxing’s son Yunquan, in the Kaiyun era, was magistrate of Fushi; removed, he lived at home.
proposals.after: Wanjin’s son Yunquan, in the Kaiyun era, was magistrate of Fushi; removed, he lived at home.
proposals.reason: Chinese 萬金子允權 names Wanjin as father; literal wrongly says Wanxing.

proposals.before: Tao was in his post seven years; of the Tang imperial tombs within his territory he opened them all, took the gold and treasure stored there—and of them Zhaoling was the most secure; Tao went down the spirit passage, saw the palace halls grand and bright, no different from the human world; in the center was the main chamber, east and west wings lined with stone couches; on the couches stone caskets held iron cases, all storing books and maps of former ages, clocks and Wang Xizhi’s traces; paper and ink were as new; Tao took them all, and they passed into the world—only Qianling, in wind and rain, could not be opened.
proposals.after: Tao was in his post seven years; of the Tang imperial tombs within his territory he opened them all, took the gold and treasure stored there—and of them Zhaoling was the most secure; Tao went down the spirit passage, saw the palace halls grand and bright, no different from the human world; in the center was the main chamber, east and west wings lined with stone couches; on the couches stone caskets held iron cases, all storing books and maps of former ages, Zhong Yao’s and Wang Xizhi’s calligraphy traces; paper and ink were as new; Tao took them all, and they passed into the world—only Qianling, in wind and rain, could not be opened.
proposals.reason: 鐘、王筆跡 is the Zhong–Wang calligraphy pair (鍾繇、王羲之); literal clocks misreads 鐘/鍾.

proposals.before: When Zhuangzong destroyed Liang, Tao came from Xu to court, bribed Empress Liu through the actor Jing Jin, and won her word. Zhuangzong favored him lavishly and renamed him Li Shaogong.
proposals.after: When Zhuangzong destroyed Liang, Tao came from Xu to court, bribed Empress Liu through the actor Jing Jin, and won her word. Zhuangzong favored him lavishly and renamed him Li Shaochong.
proposals.reason: Li Shaochong is the correct reading of the bestowed name; idiomatic Shaogong misreads the final character.
